title: Great app, but I have two suggestions
body:
I have just started using this app after my old reminder app stopped being supported due to the death of the developer. 

Overall this is a great app, but I would love to have the ability to assign different categories and colours to my reminders like I could with my old app. 

The other suggestion I have relates to the available alert sounds.... there is a massive choice of different melodies (and volumes) that run for 1 to 3 seconds.  But really only 7 different melodies that are of a longer duration (and of those, 4 are too loud for everyday use).

title: good for neurodivergent people especially
body: This app has a great design for people who can't handle too much busyness. It also has a critical function, which means the reminder nags you until you check it off., which is great for taking medications. You can set repeat times and amounts, duplicate reminders, choose from different non-offensive reminder sounds, turn on a critical alert (sound comes through even if phone is muted or on Do Not Disturb), and sync with icloud. I think it's good for people who want a simple but effective way to be reminded. Plus it has timers that you can customize (e.g., coffee steeping for 4 minutes). This is useful because I forget to take out teabags all the time.

title: As lazy an app as I feel
body:
It’s bad. Don’t bother.

Literally every single app on the market is better than this. It’s the Notes app you have on your phone, but harder to use, as you have to tap a bunch to get a due time set. No easy reorganising, no categorising by work or home or chore etc easily, no auto schedule, no relevant or decent integration... the list goes on, but my list won’t be in Due.

I’d rate it 1 star if it was free; it’s something you’d expect a uni student to make for free to bolster their portfolio with their first app. Because it’s paid, I have to write that it’s less than 0 stars.

Even better, they ask you to subscribe for their “yearly” new features. Get this - besides some recent MASSIVE updates this year (wait for it...... widgets...! Yes, I was being sarcastic), they’ve only actually delivered updates for one year out of the past half decade. So not only is this the crappiest most featureless app I’ve ever downloaded, it’s also the worst I’ve ever paid for. And I have to wait forever to request a refund.

So save yourself the effort I now have to go through.

title: When you really can't forget something
body:
I use OmniFocus for "proper" task management, but for quick one-off reminders, or things that you really can't afford to forget, I love Due.

Recurring, nagging reminders are terrific. For example, every month, it reminds me to pay rent. The alarm goes off, I'm not at a computer. I snooze it for an hour. It goes off again. I pay my rent, hit the "done" button, and the same task cycles forward a month.

Simple but brilliantly effective. So useful, it's on my home screen. Get it.

title: Frustrating
body: I bought the App and Desktop version to sync across 3 devices - iPad, iPhone and iMac - using iCloud.  In fact, I've found the iPhone and iPad repeatedly 'time out' when syncing.  Only a hard reset of the mobile device seems to trigger a satisfactory sync - inconvenient and frustrating.  It's pointless having it on iPad and iPhone because switching off the reminder alarm on one device, doesn't switch off the other, unless the second device is on with Due actually running.  Developer advice on the website suggests turning off the snooze/repeat reminder on the iPad, but that seems to defeat the purpose.  In any case the snooze feature on mobile devices can only be set to 1 minute or 1 hour - not necessarily practical.  In the end, Due isn't as user-friendly as the native iOS App 'Reminders' which comes with iPad and iPhone and which seamlessly syncs via iCal on a Mac.  If Reminders isn't good enough for you, try BusyToDo which is much more intuitive and allows for reminder categories, such as 'work', 'home' etc.

title: Avoid this if you need recurring reminders
body:
The UI design is pretty good, as others have observed. But there is one crazy shortcoming with recurring alarms that makes me regret buying this app:

Once you have set up a recurring reminder and it has 'fired', you have to go into the app and press the individual reminder's "Repeat" button - if not, the app treats it as complete and you will never hear from it again, regardless of how you set it up. I thought I must have misunderstood this because it is such a strange requirement, but the developer confirmed it (to his credit, he responded quickly).

Not even Apple's built-in reminder app does this, so it appears to be an arbitrary design choice -  and a really strange and unnecessary one.

Save your money and get "Alarmed" instead - its reminder functionality is better, it does more, its powerful basic version is free and the in-app upgrade is cheaper than Due.

author: Drebin893

title: Good app
body:
It is easy to use and great that it works without a network connection when you are on the plane or roaming overseas. 

Some of the features are a little confusing though. Like the "quick delay" symbols that represent 10 minutes, 1 hour, 1 day etc are not really intuitive. I also find that it's easy to accidentally click on the "completed/tick" when I really want to edit the event.
author: YIMG2868

title: Simply Awesome!
body:
Due is the missing link on the iPhone. It is so simple in its concept yet so amazingly functional it has become my most used app!

The ease in which I can set (and postpone tasks and reminders) helps me organize my day and keep the wife off my back! Thanks Due!!
author: benandelissa

title: Light-weight yet feature packed!
body: Very well designed app I use everyday.
author: RyanAspire

title: A great app that isn't a gimick
body: A well thought out and often used app.
author: Stop the train

title: Glorious
body:
A great little companion for the forgetful mind. Due makes it easy to remind myself with only about 15-20 seconds taken to add a reminder.

Keep on task with Due. You won't regret it. Promise!

title: Great except for alarms
body: This app has excellent functionality for what it does. I would like to give it 5 stars but the sounds it ships with are so grating I doubt I'll use it as much as it otherwise deserves.
author: dagaz

title: Perfect
body: After using Things for a long time, it was still hard to sort out appointment times and other time-critical moments. Then I found this app. It is the perfect complement. Adding items is super fast and when it is tine the app doesn't let you rest until the item is done, postponed or canceled. I love it. It has simplified my life and become one of my essential apps on the home page.

title: Great app!

title: Very streamlined
body:
Has a good GUI and ease of use. Everything is great... But the price :) 
Thanks for a great app
author: Gmtailz

title: Adds a little oomph to alarms and timers
body:
Easy to use with a great clean interface. Favours people who set up multiple repeating alarms. 

Only missing feature is to set alarms based on days (ie. Mondays and Thursdays). However can be achieved manually with easy using the quick bar.

title: Great App
body: This is a great app - a ToDo/Reminder with alarm alerts and snooze. My only suggestion would be to include an additional notes field - sometimes it is handy to be able to include additional information. All in all a great App!!

title: Interesting approach to handling To Do items
body: I'd give it 5 stars if i could set a secondary alarm before an item is due. A simple way to group items would be very useful, too. Otherwise pretty good effort - I like.

title: One of the best apps on the iPhone.
body: This has to be my most used app on my iPhone. Great functionality, simple to use interface and most of all, it helps me to keep on top of what I have to do for the day. Five stars!
